name: Yvonne Ste. Claire
languages: French (perfect, Parisian-taught, which she uses to say rude things at dinner)
equipment: Evening clothes: the Queen of Oneiros's gown, white satin sewn with seed pearls and silver bullion, and a mantle of silver lamé eleven feet long, which is at the Municipal Auditorium under guard until Tuesday
Good suit, grey, for classes at Newcomb College
Derringer (her grandfather's, a silver-mounted Remington, taken from his desk drawer on Saturday without asking), 2 rounds loaded, in her handbag
A key to the Ste. Claire Marine Ways office building on Jourdan Avenue, from her father's spare ring
The Krewe of Oneiros 1946 parade programme, with the float list: eighteen floats, the theme A Voyage to the Bottom of Dreams, float fourteen The Leviathan
A notebook of her own: everything her father has said on the telephone since Friday, in French
Disguise kit (theatrical, from the Newcomb dramatic club)
features: Doors Open (Old Money origin: doormen, club secretaries and private secretaries let her through unless told not to; advantage on Society checks among the wealthy; disadvantage on Streetwise checks below the tracks until she has spent a scene showing she can be trusted)

The Long Con (Grifter: in downtime she can build a cover identity in a day for $20; she can keep two; in a prepared cover she has advantage on Deception, Performance and Persuasion to keep it up. Her one cover so far is Miss Yvette Daunis, a Newcomb girl doing a sociology paper on the shipyards, which has fooled no one in the Seventh Ward)

Cheap Shot (Grifter: once per turn, +2d6 damage to one creature she hits with a finesse Melee weapon or a Sidearm if she has advantage, if another enemy of the target is within 5 ft of it, or if the target believed a lie she told it in the last minute)
Quick Hands (Grifter, 2nd level: a bonus action each turn to Dash, Disengage, Hide or make one Sleight of Hand check)
Racket: Roper (Grifter, 3rd level: a person she has talked to for 10 minutes treats her as a friend until given a reason not to, and will do a favor that costs them nothing without a check)

Family Name (Society Heir background: invitations, tables and an audience with most of the city's rich and powerful, who assume she is one of them. On Mardi Gras night she is the Queen of Oneiros, and every door in the Municipal Auditorium opens for her)

personality.traits: I am charming by training and honest by temperament, which makes me a dreadful liar until I am angry. I ask too many questions at dinner. I can curtsey to a duke and drive a truck, and I would rather do the second.
personality.ideals: My family built half of this city and took the other half. I want to know what we actually are, and then I want to decide whether I am still one of us.
personality.bonds: My grandfather, Honoré, whom I love more than anyone, and who taught me to read a balance sheet at nine and to never ask what was under it. My father, Lucien, who is weak and kind and frightened, and whom I am beginning to understand I must protect from himself. My mother, who is in Biloxi pretending none of this is happening.
personality.flaws: I have never paid for anything in my life and I do not know what things cost, including people. I want to be forgiven for being a Ste. Claire, and I sometimes mistake being forgiven for doing something.

appearance: A slight, pale, dark-eyed girl of twenty with her grandfather's long nose and her mother's mouth, black hair worn short against her family's wishes, ink on her second finger and a habit of biting her lip when she is thinking. In a grey Newcomb suit she looks like a student; in the Queen's gown she looks like a portrait that has decided to leave.
backstory: Yvonne Marie-Claire Ste. Claire is the only child of Lucien Ste. Claire, president of Ste. Claire Marine Ways, and the only grandchild of Honoré, who founded it, and she has been told since she was six that she would one day be Queen of Carnival for the Krewe of Oneiros, as her grandmother was in 1903 and her mother in 1924. This year, the first Carnival since the war, she is. She is also a senior at Newcomb College, writing a thesis in economics on wartime shipbuilding in the Gulf that her professor thinks too political and her grandfather thinks charming. In the course of it she has read things in the yard's public filings that do not add up, and on Saturday 2 March, at the house on Esplanade Avenue, she heard her father on the library telephone say 'I never told anyone to touch him, Emile, I told you to find the papers', and her grandfather, an hour later, on the same telephone, say to someone 'My son is a fool, Achille, not a murderer, and I will not see him tried for it'. She took her grandfather's pistol from his desk drawer that night, and she does not know why. On Sunday she will go looking for whoever is asking about Marcel Fontenot, and she will find the party.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Yvonne is the party's door into the old-money world and the Krewe of Oneiros, and she is never only that. She has her own question (what did my family do?) and her own choice to make in cs-scenario-004 (what do I do about it?), and the party cannot make it for her. She brings the party into the yard office with her father's key (cs-scenario-002), tells them which krewe member rides on float fourteen (Clue E4), and gets them into the Oneiros ball and the captain's room on Mardi Gras night (cs-scenario-003). She is brave, impulsive and badly out of her depth below Canal Street, and the GM should let the Seventh Ward characters be politely unimpressed by her until she does something real. She is the Queen of Carnival: on Mardi Gras night she rides the queen's float and holds court at the ball, and she cannot simply leave without everyone in the city noticing.
dmNotes.voice: Quick, clear, educated, a little breathless when she is excited; switches into French with her family and when she wants to be rude. She says "one" when she means "I" when she is nervous, and stops when she notices.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: the truth about Marcel Fontenot's death, because she is terrified her father did it. Secondary: protect her grandfather, and, increasingly, her father. Tertiary: be someone other than the Queen of Oneiros by Ash Wednesday.
dmNotes.secrets: She overheard both halves of the cover-up (Clue H3): her father telling Emile Gravier he never ordered anyone touched, and her grandfather telling Captain Lebeau that Lucien is a fool and not a murderer. She has not understood it yet: she thinks it means her father did it and her grandfather is protecting him. It actually means that each of them thinks the other did it. Second: she knows that Commander Thaddeus Pruett rides masked on float fourteen, The Leviathan, because her father got him into the krewe in 1944 and she seated him at the krewe supper (Clue E4). Third: her thesis notes contain the yard's public wage filings with the State, which show 412 'colored helpers' paid at seventy-eight cents in 1944 and no Black welders at all.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: eager, grateful and a little patronising, until someone tells her so. Toward Solange: she knows exactly who Solange is (her father is not discreet) and is icily polite, then curious. Toward Vincent Lamarque: she has known him since she was a child at Oneiros suppers and is relieved to see him. Toward Theo and Octave: she wants their approval, and knows she has not earned it. Toward Commander Pruett: she has always disliked him and never known why.
